beats.lead: The first computer virus was not built to harm anything
beats.text: It was built to say hello.
beats.note: In 1971, a program called Creeper moved between machines on ARPANET, the internet's ancestor, and printed a message rather than deleting or stealing anything.

beats.name: Bob Thomas
beats.role: At BBN, wrote Creeper for the PDP-10 operating system TENEX. It displayed: I'M THE CREEPER, CATCH ME IF YOU CAN.

beats.context: The absolute most computers Creeper could ever infect, because that was the entire population of TENEX machines then on ARPANET.

beats.lead: It also caused the second thing it's famous for
beats.text: It got hunted down on purpose.
beats.note: Ray Tomlinson, who separately built the first networked email, wrote a program called Reaper in 1972 whose only job was to find Creeper and delete it. The first virus. The first antivirus.

beats.text: The internet's first infection topped out at 28 machines.

beats.line: It just wanted to say it had been there.
